title: Embedding the length-machine computation
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be finite Boolean Turing machines with positive numbers of work tapes, and choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$. Let $w,s,u,v,z$ be Boolean words and let $t>0$. Suppose that, when started on input $w$ in state $d_e$ with $v$ on its first work tape and all its other tapes blank, $D$ is not in state $d_x$ at any time $j$ with $0<j<t$, and at time $t$ it is in state $d_x$ with $z$ on its first work tape and all its other tapes blank. Then the controller started in its length-start state with candidate $s$ and bank words $u,v$ reaches length state $d_x$ with candidate $s$ and bank words $u,z$ at time $t$, and its state is not the anchor at any time $j\le t$.
hypotheses_covered: $c_e,c_x$ are states of $C$; $d_e,d_x$ are states of $D$
The run of $D$ from the specified seam is not in state $d_x$ for $0<j<t$
At time $t$, that run equals the specified seam with state $d_x$ and result word $z$
replaced:
If the suffix-length machine, started on its canonical seam carrying the
prepared suffix, reaches its exit seam with result word $z$ in $t > 0$
steps with no interior exit-state visit, then $t$ controller steps from the
length-start seam install $z$ in the length bank while preserving the
candidate and the already installed width word; the trace avoids the
anchor.
